passage:
A weather chart showing a huge storm spread online. Many people became frightened and bought extra supplies.
Meteorologists explained that the chart was only one possible model from many days before the storm. It was not a final forecast.
News programs then taught viewers how to read forecast uncertainty.
Some people still complained, but others learned to wait for official updates.
The event showed that raw information without context can mislead. A dramatic image may be technically real and still easy to misunderstand.
Weather science is not only about prediction. It is also about communication. People need to know what a chart means before fear fills the empty spaces.

glossary.translation: 從技術上來說；技術性地
